checks.finding: No road right-of-way touches this parcel in Franklin County's right-of-way layer. The nearest mapped road, Seaman Rd, is about 107 m away in the county engineer's road layer. The Franklin County Auditor lists the parcel as "SEAMAN RD REAR".
checks.limitation: These layers show mapped right-of-way and road centerlines. They do not show recorded easements, private lanes, or other legal access, so they cannot establish whether the parcel has access.

responsibleParty.role: Title reviewer, then county zoning office

checks.nextAction: Title review should look for recorded legal access to Seaman Rd, such as an easement. Franklin County zoning should confirm how the lot could meet road frontage: §302.042 requires 150 feet on a public street or frontage on an approved private street, and §302.0391 lets a private lane count only for back land without public water or sewer, dedicated on a subdivision plat approved by the Franklin County Planning Commission, with a homeowners' association to maintain it.

checks.finding: Franklin County's zoning map places the whole parcel in the Rural (R) district. The parcel is in unincorporated Pleasant Township, where the county administers zoning. The Rural District permits one-family dwellings (§302.021) with at least 2.5 acres per dwelling (§302.041); the Franklin County Auditor lists 3.015 legal acres. A dwelling lot must also abut an improved, dedicated, publicly maintained street right-of-way for at least 150 feet, or front on an approved private street (§302.042).
checks.limitation: A zoning map and a lot size are not a zoning certificate or a building permit. The county's right-of-way layer shows no road touching this parcel (see access), so whether it meets the §302.042 frontage requirement needs county zoning review. If a building, driveway, or septic system would go near the stream, the Big Darby Creek Watershed riparian setback, which covers about 5% of the parcel in the county's stream-buffer layer, would also apply.

checks.finding: FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer maps the whole parcel in Zone X, area of minimal flood hazard. The zone comes from Franklin County's FIRM panel 39049C0290K, effective June 17, 2008. Madison County's panel 39097C0190E, effective November 16, 2023, also covers this location.
checks.limitation: Zone X is not a guarantee against flooding or a flood-insurance determination, and FEMA can revise the map after this date.

checks.finding: USDA NRCS SSURGO (Esri Living Atlas copy) maps 46.05% of the parcel as map unit Ko (Kokomo silty clay loam, 0 to 2 percent slopes), 38.31% as map unit CrB (Crosby silt loam, Southern Ohio Till Plain, 2 to 6 percent slopes), and 15.64% as map unit CeB2 (Celina silt loam, 2 to 6 percent slopes, eroded). All three are rated “Very limited” for septic-tank absorption fields. These published soil limitations do not establish that an on-site sewage system is feasible.
checks.limitation: The rating describes a map unit's dominant soil condition for septic-tank absorption fields. It does not confirm sewer availability, choose a system or drain-field location, account for every site condition, or replace a permit and an on-site soil evaluation.
